item.title: British Police Try to Track Down Theft of 70,000 Pints Worth of Guinness Stout
item.description: British police have a stout task ahead: recovering 70,000 pints worth of stolen Guinness. “We will settle for nothing less than the full recovery of all the items stolen.” Related: Pabst Blue Ribbon Offers $20K Reward for Missing Beer From Truck Heist The Guinness had been destined for pubs, but was snatched Monday night by two drivers who pulled up to an industrial park in Runcorn and hauled away the trailers containing about 800 barrels of stout. this is real and we are deadly serious.” Police valued the Pabst theft from a Southern California warehouse at $70,000 and the company offered a $20,000 reward for information leading to the recovery of the stolen suds.

item.title: BASF Sues Apple in US, Says iPhones Infringe Face Authentication Patents
item.description: BASF sued Apple on Thursday, accusing the iPhone maker of infringing the German chemical company’s patented face authentication technology in many iPhone and iPad models. The complaint said Apple did not employ BASF’s patented technology when it launched face authentication, known as Face ID, in 2017 with the iPhone X, but now uses it in a variety of iPhone 15, iPhone 16, iPhone 17, iPad Pro and other products. “Apple knew or should have known of the high probability that updating its iPhones and iPads to incorporate Face ID using material and skin detection” infringed seven trinamiX patents, causing “substantial damages and irreparable injury,” the complaint said.

item.title: Cedar Trace ILS bolsters its leadership. Fergus Reynolds to become CEO, adds new hire
item.description: Cedar Trace ILS, the Bermuda-based specialist insurance-linked securities arm of Cedar Trace Capital Management Group and closely linked to Mereo Insurance, has announced a range of leadership promotions and a strategic hire, which includes Fergus Reynolds being promoted to CEO. item.title: Abundant reinsurance capital a “window” to diversify before conditions shift: Madea, CEO HCMA
item.description: Today’s abundant reinsurance and insurance-linked securities capital levels presents the sector with a window of opportunity to diversify its capital stack and secure longer-duration solutions, before the market inevitably shifts again, Jarad Madea, CEO of Howden Capital Markets & Advisory told us in an interview. Going on to explain that, “Today’s abundant capital is a window to secure long-duration solutions before conditions shift, including multi-year reinsurance capacity, catastrophe bonds, casualty sidecars, or Funds at Lloyd’s. Most companies pour resources into growth strategies and give too little attention to what happens when conditions turn.” Madea urges his clients to start with an honest audit of their capital base and sources, to identify how diversified it really is and where that can be improved upon.

item.title: Abundant capacity and volatility are helping the re/insurance market innovate: Aon’s Lyons
item.description: “But what I think makes us most excited about this renewal season is that that increase in capacity, in capital and increase in volatility is also really driving increases in innovation.” During the briefing, Lyons reviewed market conditions for each line of business and highlighted the corresponding innovations emerging within them. The executive, who serves as CEO of Bermuda and Global Head of Products, argued that unprecedented capacity across nearly every line of business is a key opening for cedents to reset and future-proof their programmes against market volatility. In property, reinsurers continue to generate strong double-digit return on equity (ROE), with pricing still holding above 30% over the index at the height of the stock market, Lyons notes.

item.title: Cyber reinsurance market to shift focus to strategic deployment: Ariel Re’s Carr
item.description: Ample capacity and sustained competitive pricing will characterise the cyber reinsurance market, but the core discussion is shifting from sheer volume to strategic deployment, Daniel Carr, Head of Cyber Underwriting at Ariel Re, stated in a recent interview with Reinsurance News. We expect the discussion to move beyond simply how much cyber reinsurance is available towards how cedents allocate that capacity across the loss distribution.” This reassessment is driving a shift in buyer behaviour ahead of the January 1, 2027, renewals, where Carr anticipates a “more deliberate approach” centred on structure, attachment, and event definition rather than a dramatic pricing shift. According to Carr, as the reinsurance industry meets at Rendez-Vous de Septembre (RVS) 2026 in Monte Carlo, the question for the market is no longer how much capacity exists, but where along the loss distribution cedents choose to deploy it.

item.title: MS Re’s Bruniecki says retentions to hold as attachment points stay disciplined
item.description: Especially, as casualty is such a diverse universe where risks are big and very volatile, I do think risk and rating go more hand in hand.” Turning to terms and conditions, and specifically attachment points, Bruniecki argued that discipline throughout the risk chain is what has kept retentions intact since the market reset of 2022. People will have to get disciplined in their underwriting because we cannot support business which is below technically adequate levels.” Casualty, in Bruniecki’s assessment, remains a different story, with rate adequacy still an open question given how varied the class of business is. I do think for the most part retentions will stay in place.

item.title: Seattle Times, Newsday Sue OpenAI, Microsoft, Alleging Copyright Infringement
item.description: The Seattle Times and Newsday sued OpenAI and Microsoft on Friday, alleging in federal court that the tech companies copied the newspapers’ journalism without permission to train their AI systems. A spokesperson for Microsoft, based near Seattle in Washington state, said in an email: “While we’re surprised by the lawsuit, we appreciate the importance of local journalism and we’re always happy to sit down and explore solutions to this type of dispute.” The Seattle Times and Newsday are seeking an order requiring the destruction of copies of their works as well as training datasets or AI models incorporating them. The lawsuit echoes a case filed by the New York Times in 2023, which accused OpenAI and Microsoft of using millions of newspaper articles without permission to train OpenAI’s popular chatbot.

item.title: Viewpoint: Reinsurance Market to Experience Further Softening, M&A on Ample Capacity
item.description: Challenging Renewals as Softening Continues; Terms Weaken Fitch expects highly competitive market conditions in most property and specialty lines to drive further market softening in 2027. A materially elevated loss experience would likely be required to change the softening market trend. The global reinsurance market maintains a very strong capital position that has benefitted from favorable earnings in recent years, with solid underwriting profits and resilient investment returns.

item.title: Ransomware Trends in 2026 for Cyber Insurers
item.description: The biggest ransomware trends in 2026 are the shift from file encryption toward data theft, stolen credentials, cloud and infrastructure compromise, AI-assisted activity and cyber insurance accumulation risk. The most important ransomware trends in 2026 involve attackers moving beyond file encryption and targeting the identities, data, infrastructure and shared systems that organizations depend on to operate and recover. For cyber insurers, these developments make the complete loss chain increasingly important when assessing ransomware insurance claims, underwriting exposure and portfolio accumulation.

item.title: Why Human Audits of AI Decisions Fail
item.description: Ask an organization how it governs an AI-assisted process and, sooner or later, someone will say that a human reviews the decisions. Eventually, the organization can point to a documented human-review process while the overwhelming majority of AI-assisted decisions pass through without meaningful scrutiny. As AI scales, insurers relying on sampling to audit AI decisions may be kidding themselves.

item.title: Aviva launches hybrid fronting offering for MGAs
item.description: Aviva has launched a hybrid fronting offering for larger, established MGAs through its Global Corporate & Specialty business. As demand grows for partners that can support international, multi-class programmes, our hybrid model gives MGAs, brokers and reinsurers a single route into Aviva’s global reach, specialist underwriting expertise and financial strength. The offering combines fronting capacity with risk retention and is designed for multi-country, multi-line insurance programs generating at least £20 million in gross written premium.

item.title: Price adequacy is essential as ILS expands into casualty, specialty, and cyber: Artex’s Faries
item.description: As the ILS market expands its reach across casualty, specialty, and cyber, maintaining price adequacy remains a critical boundary for market growth. I think we have to watch the price adequacy and the softening to make sure that we don’t dip below a threshold that will cause investors to think about whether to deploy their capital elsewhere, but I don’t think we’re there yet.” As the ILS space continues to tap into hybrid, casualty, and specialty structures, operational complexity is also rising sharply. But it’s always a supply, demand, and return equation.” Turning to casualty, Faries explained that she sees sustained momentum ahead, adding: “Overall, I think there is further opportunity in casualty so we expect that growth to continue into 2027.” On specialty lines, Faries pointed to key market mechanisms facilitating institutional capital deployment: “Regarding specialty, we are involved in London Bridge 2 in the UK, which is the vehicle that efficiently delivers capital supporting Lloyd’s Syndicates.

item.title: Swiss Re expects to remain a meaningful participant in alternative capital: Baertschi
item.description: Speaking today at Swiss Re’s briefing at RVS 2026 in Monte Carlo, Urs Baertschi, Chief Executive Officer, of P&C Reinsurance, underscored the importance of the reinsurers third-party capital markets focused Alternative Capital Partners (ACP) division, and stated that Swiss Re expects to continue to be a “meaningful participant in that market.” During Swiss Re’s media briefing at RVS today, Baertschi stressed the overall importance of the reinsurance industry having a strong capital base. The rest we think of as alternative capital as well.” Baertschi continued: “Alternative capital is an important part of the capital stack, and the opportunities that insurance companies and buyers of this kind of protection have, and it also very importantly supports the traditional reinsurance capacity.” In light of this, we asked senior executives what the reinsurer’s plans were for growing its Alternative Capital Partners division into 2027. Earlier this year, Swiss Re launched a new Alternative Capital Solutions unit to encompass its activities in ILS and retrocessional hedging and execution.

item.title: Cat bonds and casualty sidecars buoyant, but investors still don’t like surprises: Josefs, S&P
item.description: At the S&P Global Ratings briefing in Monte Carlo at the RVS, Maren Josefs, Credit Analyst at the company explained that the big stories in insurance-linked securities has been catastrophe bonds and casualty sidecars this year, but she cautioned the market to remember that investors still don’t like surprises. The protection gap between economic and insured losses is still widening across the globe, and at the same time, we have these new risks coming from geopolitics, climate, and technology advances, especially AI.” Moving on Josefs highlighted the two biggest sources of growth, as catastrophe bonds and reinsurance sidecars. Josefs stated, “The two main stories have been the cat bond market and the sidecars, especially on the casualty side.

item.title: Moody’s warns uncertainty around emerging risks could constrain re/insurance growth
item.description: “Insurers may want to tap into growth in emerging markets or new areas of risk, but uncertainty is high, and too many insurers don’t have the tools to understand the risks and grow meaningfully into these new areas.” Speaking at their firm’s briefing in Monte Carlo today, Brandan Holmes, SVP at Moody’s Ratings, and Joe Melly, Head of Casualty and Financial Lines at Moody’s Insurance Solutions, warned that insurers are navigating an increasingly interconnected and uncertain emerging-risk landscape. In his opening remarks at the briefing, held at the 68th edition of the Rendez-Vous de Septembre (RVS), Holmes suggested that the centre of gravity on insurance emerging risks is shifting.

item.title: Compre completes retrospective structured ADC transaction with Lloyd’s syndicate
item.description: Compre Group Holdings Limited (Compre), the Bermuda-domiciled international specialty reinsurance group, has reached an agreement on a retrospective structured adverse development cover (ADC) transaction with a Lloyd’s syndicate. Rachel Bardon, Chief Underwriting Officer at Compre, said, “This transaction is a strong example of how we are continuing to evolve our retrospective proposition to meet clients’ changing capital and balance sheet needs. The transaction covers the syndicate’s 2023 and prior Years of Account on a whole-account basis, spanning a multi-line portfolio of property and casualty business and assumed reinsurance, with subject reserves of approximately £200 million.

item.title: Closing cyber protection gap a major business opportunity: Munich Re
item.description: Speaking during the firm’s briefing at the 2026 Rendez-Vous de Septembre (RVS) in Monte Carlo, Stefan Golling, a Member of the Board of Management of Munich Re, suggested that the industry has not done enough to close the significant cyber protection gap, while also flagging the major business opportunity in doing so as Munich Re looks to maintain its position as a market leader in the growing sector. He went on, “Closing the cyber protection gap is a major business opportunity, but it’s also our responsibility as an industry if we want to live up to the picture of being the immune system for our customers. Golling observed that much of the growth in cyber has come over the past 24 to 36 months and, with rates having softened, said he believes the industry has not done enough to close the significant protection gap.

item.title: Experian launches credit card app on ChatGPT

item.title: Insurance Claims Lose the Paper Chase as AI Gets to Work
item.description: Insurance claims have always been document-heavy, time-sensitive, and prone to fraud. A Swiss Re article written by Florian Maurer, chief D&T officer Corporate Solutions, and Vincent Plantard, GL head of Performance, Analytics and Delivery at Claims Corporate Solutions, describes how SwissRe built and deployed ClaimsGenAI to automate its corporate insurance claims handling process. SwissRe’s annual corporate insurance claims now exceed 40,000, creating a clear need for a step change in how the company manages growing caseloads.

item.title: Hannover Re on steady ILS growth path with Capital Partners after first capital raise: Silke Sehm
item.description: “HCP has successfully written additional non-proportional catastrophe business in 2026 under its first third-party capital mandate, so we are on a steady growth path within our broader ILS offering framework.” Regarding how much capital was raised, Sehm said it was a “lower three-digit million number” Michael Eberhardt, CEO Hannover Re Capital Partners and Head of P&C, Hannover Re Bermuda, said: “Yes, so we are fully aligned with the investor base, and also we have a governance structure around it. Speaking in Monte Carlo this morning, Hannover Re Executive Board Member Silke Sehm noted that the company’s ILS management platform, Hannover Re Capital Partners, successfully wrote additional non-proportional catastrophe business in 2026 under its first third-party capital mandate, with a “lower three-digit million number” of capital raised. Recall that the global reinsurer launched its Hannover Re Capital Partners operation at the beginning of 2026 and in advance of that had explained the rationale as putting in place a missing piece of Hannover Re’s ILS offering .

item.title: ILS will return to the cyber conversation in time. AI risk a future factor: Baker, CyberCube
item.description: Speaking with Artemis around the time of the Monte Carlo Reinsurance Rendez-vous event, Baker said that investor engagement on understanding cyber risk and readying themselves to invest in the cyber ILS asset class continues. Baker of CyberCube explained why the cyber cat bond market has been quiet of late, highlighting the economics, “The soft market means traditional reinsurance capacity exists at lower prices, which decreases the general need to reach towards the ILS market for risk and capital management. “On top of that, cyber balance sheets are not yet a significant driver in a lot of carrier or reinsurance companies’ overall risk, so time and resources get spent elsewhere first right now.” She continued to say that investor interest is not a limiting factor, “That said, from what we can see there is more investor demand than sponsor supply, so that’s not holding back the market at this time.

item.title: Catastrophe bond fund UCITS Index delivers 1.24% average return in August: Plenum
item.description: Catastrophe bond fund structured in the UCITS investment format delivered their strongest month of performance year-to-date through the August days of record, averaging 1.24% for the period, while the 12-month rolling return average across the Plenum CAT Bond UCITS Fund Indices slipped a little further to 9.82%. The average return of UCITS catastrophe bond funds is the strongest so far in 2026 for a reporting period, since the nearest last end of month reporting of this Index, on July 31st through to August 28th 2026, at 1.24%. On the back of this, the average year-to-date performance of the UCITS catastrophe bond fund strategies rose from 4.09 % as of July 31st, to now 5.38% as of August 28th 2026.

item.title: PwC RVS: Convex’s Brand says strong carriers can thrive in soft phase of cycle
item.description: Speaking at PwC’s annual breakfast briefing during this year’s RVS in Monte Carlo, Paul Brand, Chief Executive Officer of international specialty insurer and reinsurer Convex, suggested that carriers with relevance, resilience and efficiency do absolutely fine during this phase of the cycle. Rather than viewing softer conditions as a uniform challenge, Brand suggested that the cycle tends to expose differences in the quality and positioning of carriers. “The very interesting thing about the soft phase of the cycle is that this is the point in time when outcomes actually disperse.

item.title: Underlying need for reinsurance protection continues to grow: Swiss Re
item.description: Urs Baertschi, Chief Executive Officer, Property & Casualty Reinsurance, Swiss Re, commented, “The underlying need for protection continues to grow as the risk landscape evolves and becomes more interconnected. According to Swiss Re’s modelled scenarios, insured losses could reach around USD 320 billion in a 2026 peak loss scenario, highlighting that reinsurance protection against low-frequency, high-severity events is important. At the 68th annual meeting of the reinsurance industry in Monte Carlo, Swiss Re, an industry giant, has emphasised that growing natural catastrophe risk remains a significant driver of reinsurance demand.

item.title: Cyber reinsurance buyers willing to explore higher cessions at Jan 1 renewals: Marsh Re’s Cordonnier
item.description: Anthony Cordonnier, Global Co-Head of Cyber, Managing Director at reinsurance broker Marsh Re, said a meaningful shift that is beginning to appear is a willingness among some buyers to explore higher cessions at the 1 January 2027 cyber renewals. In an interview with Reinsurance News around the annual meeting of the reinsurance industry in Monte Carlo, Cordonnier explained that buyers of cyber reinsurance are exploring higher cessions as they reassess whether their current programmes are appropriately sized for the risks they are running. At the key 1.1 2027 cyber renewals, Cordonnier noted that buyers with the widest range of options are likely to be those that have invested properly in understanding their exposure and can articulate a coherent underwriting strategy to the market.

item.title: Viewpoint: How the Federal Ban on Intoxicating Hemp Products Will Reshape Risk and Coverage
item.description: I have been writing about the insurance risks of intoxicating hemp products since 2021, when delta-8 THC gummies first started showing up in convenience stores and gas stations across the country. There is real momentum behind some of these efforts, and even the White House has signaled support for protecting non-intoxicating hemp products from the ban’s overreach. These products violate the spirit, if not the actual letter, of the 2018 Farm Bill, and the cannabis and hemp industries and their insurers should be wary of a government response.
